newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Telebras to be divided into four units - report.
newsitem.headline: Telebras to be divided into four units - report.

text.p: Brazilian telecommunications monopoly Telebras will be divided into four Baby Bell-like operating units the first of which could be privatized as early as 1997, the nation's communications minister was quoted as saying on Thursday in Brazil's leading financial daily.
Sergio Motta told Gazeta Mercantil that Sao Paulo state telecom operator Telesp, the country's largest operator, would be sold off before the end of this year.
The other three operating units would be privatized during 1998, Gazeta quoted Motta as saying on Wednesday at a Presidential Palace ceremony.

The palace event had been called to mark the signing of an agreement between the Communications Ministry and the National Development Bank (BNDES) for the hiring of three consulting groups to help design Brazil's new telecom regulations, the newspaper said.

The three consulting groups will propose a model for a new telecom regulating agency, a model for the opening of the telecom market and the terms for the sale of the Band A cellular market currently being exploited by Telebras, Gazeta said.
Motta said at the ceremony that his Ministry was moving ahead with the telecom deregulation process despite the fact Congress had still not voted on key deregulation legislation.
The minister, who originally hoped Congress would approve the telecom deregulation bill before the end of February, on Wednesday said he expected it to be approved by April.
